_description: Fit-scoring ENGINE calibration constants -- properties of how the scoring algorithm interprets its own output, not personal job-search preferences. Deliberately separate from data/candidate_preferences.json (gitignored, holds Jason's actual preferences: location, blocked industries, min salary, etc.). This file is tracked in git on purpose: a recalibration is a real, reviewable event, the same way a CR doc tracks a threshold change -- it shouldn't disappear into a gitignored personal-data file where the history is invisible.

score_bands.rationale: Working production floor for Stage 0. Skip below 40, Tier 2 from 40 up to 65, Tier 1 at 65+. Jason locked these numbers on 2026-08-20 (CR-093 Story 3.3). Grounded in TalentWorks real-outcome data (callback odds climb from ~40% requirement-match and plateau by ~50-60%) plus Applyr's own archive scores under this engine (5 JDs: 40/53/55/56/63). Locked means the open decision is closed, not that an Angoff or Contrasting-Groups calibration has been run. That still needs interview/no-interview labels under this engine.
score_bands.upgrade_path: When Jason applies to jobs scored under this engine and real interview outcomes come back, compare the score distribution of JDs that converted against those that didn't, and reset the floors at the real intersection (Contrasting-Groups). Do not quietly drift these numbers without that data or an explicit new decision.

weighting_model.rationale: Per data/fit_rubric_spec.html Sec. 10: the research supports the ORDERING (required outweighs preferred, direct evidence outweighs adjacent) but not these exact magnitudes. Repetition (+1, capped) and hedge-language (-1) modifiers from the same spec section are not yet implemented in code at all.
weighting_model.note: Still read as Python module constants in scripts/evidence_scale.py (_REQUIRED_WEIGHT, _PREFERRED_WEIGHT, _CONFIDENCE_MULTIPLIER), not yet wired to this file -- flagged here so the next recalibration pass moves them together with score_bands instead of finding them scattered again.
